review_notes: Read the whole file and the definitions of numEdges/graphConnected (ChipFiringWithLean/Basic.lean). Considered the duplicated loopless branches, the near-identical num_edges inl/inr simp proofs, and the hLeftCross/hRightCross blocks. Only the last is nontrivial reasoning (pulling a cut back along an embedding, applying connectivity of a factor, pushing the crossing edge forward); the others are routine simp/unfolding. The proposed lemma has not been compiled; the hypothesis for the embedding would be discharged by the existing simp lemmas num_edges_bridgeGraph_inl/inr, which is likely but unverified.

findings.problem: The proof contains two copies of the same argument, one for each factor. Each copy restricts the cut S to the factor with a filtered Finset (SL or SR), proves the restricted cut is nontrivial, applies connectedness of the factor, and transports the crossing edge back into the sum graph using the num_edges_bridgeGraph_inl/inr simp lemmas. The copies differ only in Sum.inl versus Sum.inr and G versus H. Any fix or change to the cut-pullback logic has to be made twice.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a private lemma about an arbitrary graph morphism-like map:

private theorem exists_cross_of_embedding {F K : CFGraph} (f : F.V → K.V)
    (hf : ∀ p q, 0 < numEdges F p q → 0 < numEdges K (f p) (f q))
    (hF : graphConnected F) (S : Finset K.V) {a b : F.V} (ha : f a ∈ S) (hb : f b ∉ S) :
    ∃ z ∈ S, ∃ w ∉ S, numEdges K z w > 0

Proof sketch: let T := Finset.univ.filter (fun p => f p ∈ S). Then a ∈ T and b ∉ T, so hF T ⟨a, b, _, _⟩ gives p ∈ T, q ∉ T with 0 < numEdges F p q. Return ⟨f p, _, f q, _, hf p q _⟩.

Then in graph_connected_bridgeGraph, define hLeftCross := fun a b ha hb => exists_cross_of_embedding Sum.inl (fun p q h => by simpa using h) hG S ha hb (using num_edges_bridgeGraph_inl, which is @[simp]), and hRightCross the same with Sum.inr and hH. The SL/SR lets and both 10-line blocks disappear. The existing case analysis on hx, hy, hS stays unchanged.
findings.benefit: The cut-restriction argument is stated and proved once, with an explicit hypothesis on the embedding. The main theorem then shows only the bridge case analysis. The lemma can also be reused for other gluing constructions that embed a connected factor.
